New Zealand has an extensive network of double tax agreements; applicability and treaty benefits depend on the counterparty jurisdiction, residence, income type, and treaty anti-abuse provisions. New Zealand does not provide a tax-exempt international-company regime.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Companies Act 1993, including sections 10, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 19, 20, and 189; Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 where applicable; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 (AML/CFT Act), including sections 5, 6, 10, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 57, 58, 59, 60, 61, 62, 63, 64, and 66 where the entity is a reporting entity. New Zealand has no generally applicable statutory central beneficial ownership register for companies equivalent to a public UBO register. Companies must maintain shareholder and director records and file prescribed information with the Companies Office. AML/CFT beneficial-owner identification obligations apply to reporting entities, not automatically to every company or every business. The payload's 'International Company' and 'Tax_Exempt_Zone' classifications do not describe a New Zealand statutory company or tax status; the usual limited-liability vehicle is a company incorporated under the Companies Act 1993 and resident companies are generally subject to New Zealand income tax.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: New Zealand reporting entities must apply a risk-based AML/CFT compliance programme, conduct customer due diligence and identify beneficial owners under the AML/CFT Act and applicable regulations. Enhanced due diligence applies in specified higher-risk cases, including relevant politically exposed persons under section 5 and the AML/CFT (Definitions) Regulations 2011. New Zealand reporting entities must comply with applicable New Zealand targeted financial sanctions and asset-freeze obligations, including sanctions imposed under the Russia Sanctions Act 2022 and regulations, and relevant United Nations sanctions implemented through New Zealand law. OFAC screening is not a universal New Zealand statutory requirement; it may be required by a bank, payment provider, contract, or US nexus. Stripe, Wise, and other financial institutions may apply their own sanctions and PEP screening policies. A post-production subtitle and AI voice-cloning studio is not automatically an AML/CFT reporting entity solely by conducting that business.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office online services, including the Companies Register at companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed company name must be in English or Maori, must comply with the Companies Act 1993 and Companies Register requirements, and must not be identical or almost identical to a name already reserved or registered. The Registrar may reject a name that is offensive, misleading, or otherwise prohibited by law. No general requirement mandates a parallel Maori-script name or transliteration. A name reservation is a separate step before incorporation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Names identical or almost identical to a name already reserved or registered
Names whose use would contravene the Companies Act 1993 or another enactment
Names that are offensive or otherwise unacceptable to the Registrar
Words implying a regulated status, government affiliation, or professional authority where the implication is false or the use is restricted
Restricted financial, banking, insurance, trust, or other regulated-sector terms where use would be misleading or require consent under applicable legislation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is ordinarily valid for 20 working days, not 30 calendar days. If the reservation expires, submit a new name-reservation application and pay the applicable fee. On rejection, review the Registrar's stated grounds, choose a compliant alternative or provide supporting information through the Companies Office process, and contact the Companies Office to request reconsideration or correction of an apparent factual or administrative error. The Companies Act 1993 does not establish a routine merits appeal process specifically for a name-reservation refusal; any formal challenge must be assessed under the applicable statutory review or judicial-review framework and should be confirmed with New Zealand counsel. Incorporation also requires at least one director who lives in New Zealand or lives in Australia and is a director of an Australian company.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A registered office and address for service in New Zealand are required under the Companies Act 1993. A serviced or virtual office may be acceptable if it is a genuine physical address in New Zealand at which statutory records and communications can be received and the company can meet applicable access and record-keeping requirements. A mailbox-only address is not an adequate substitute. Banks, payment processors, tax authorities, and counterparties may require evidence of real business operations, management, and address and may decline a virtual-office-only profile. No tax-exempt-zone treatment follows from using a New Zealand registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No reliable public statistic quantifies unannounced on-site inspection likelihood for this business type. New Zealand Companies Office incorporation does not ordinarily entail a routine physical inspection. AML/CFT supervisors may inspect reporting entities, but this studio is not automatically a reporting entity on the stated facts. Treat the likelihood as low for an ordinary non-regulated post-production studio, with no defensible numeric percentage; risk increases if the company becomes a reporting entity, presents inconsistent address or operating information, or is selected for regulatory or tax compliance activity.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1981-82 (Cook Islands), as consolidated and amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Acts 1991-92, 1996-97, 2003, 2009-10 and 2011-12 (the 'ICA'). Core provisions: Part II, ss. 4-16 (incorporation, Articles of Incorporation, registered office, registered agent); s. 22 (share capital); s. 52 (unanimous written resolutions in lieu of a meeting); s. 129 (statutory exemption of international companies from income tax). The Cook Islands is a self-governing territory in free association with New Zealand and forms part of the Realm of New Zealand; the company's legal existence and tax-exempt status are recognized throughout the Realm.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) of the Cook Islands, Rarotonga; filing conducted via the FSC e-Registry online portal and through a FSC-licensed Registered Agent.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation for an International Company (Form IC-1), accompanied by Form IC-2 (Consents of Directors) and Form IC-3 (Consent and Acceptance of the Registered Agent); the Certificate of Incorporation is issued by the Registrar upon registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no minimum authorized capital. The ICA permits shares with or without par value, in any currency, and shares may be issued fully paid or partly paid. No escrow account, capital deposit, or local bank balance requirement is imposed on an international company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTIONS OF [COMPANY NAME] INTERNATIONAL COMPANY (the 'Company'), adopted by written consent of the sole incorporator and first directors pursuant to s. 52 of the International Companies Act 1981-82 (Cook Islands), as amended (the 'Act').

WHEREAS the Articles of Incorporation of the Company were executed and delivered to the Registrar of International Companies for registration on [DATE];

WHEREAS the Company has been validly incorporated and the undersigned constitute the first Board of Directors;

NOW THEREFORE IT IS RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

1. ADOPTION OF CONSTITUTIVE DOCUMENTS: The Articles of Incorporation, as registered, and the Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar thereunder, are ratified and adopted in their entirety as the constitutive documents of the Company.

2. SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT OF SHARES: The subscription by the sole incorporator for 100 ordinary shares of no par value, representing the entire issued share capital of the Company, is approved; such shares are allotted fully paid to the subscriber; and the entries made in the Register of Members are confirmed.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE AND REGISTERED AGENT: The registered office of the Company is established at [Registered Office Address], Rarotonga, Cook Islands, being the office of [Name of Licensed Registered Agent]; such agent is appointed as the registered agent of the Company pursuant to s. 16 of the Act; and the registered agent is authorized to accept service of process and statutory notices on behalf of the Company.

4. APPOINTMENT OF DIRECTORS AND OFFICERS: [Name 1], [Name 2] and [Name 3] are appointed as the first directors of the Company. [Name 1] is appointed President and Chief Executive Officer; [Name 2] is appointed Secretary; and [Name 3] is appointed Treasurer and Chief Financial Officer, each with the powers, duties and authorities conferred by the Act and the Articles.

5. TAX-EXEMPT STATUS: The Company shall operate strictly as an international company under the Act, transacting exclusively with persons who are not residents of the Cook Islands and deriving no income from sources within the Cook Islands, so as to qualify for the statutory exemption from income tax pursuant to s. 129 of the Act; the officers are directed to maintain records sufficient to evidence such exemption.

6. COMMENCEMENT OF BUSINESS: The business of the Company, being the provision of automated subtitle transcription, AI voice cloning, dubbing, and digital post-production services to clients worldwide, is authorized; and management may enter into all client agreements, software licenses, and platform terms (including, without limitation, Stripe and Wise payment service agreements) ancillary thereto.

7. BANKING AND PAYMENT RAILS: The officers are authorized, for and on behalf of the Company, to open, operate, designate and close bank accounts, digital wallet accounts, merchant processing accounts and payment rail accounts with financial institutions in any jurisdiction, and to execute all account documentation, resolutions and online banking mandates necessary therefor.

8. CORPORATE SEAL: A common corporate seal, an impression of which has been affixed to these resolutions, is adopted; the Secretary is directed to maintain custody of the seal and to affix it only upon the resolution of the Board.

9. AUTHORIZATIONS AND INDEMNITY: The directors and officers are authorized to execute, deliver, acknowledge or file any and all instruments, certificates, notices or tax declarations required by the laws of any jurisdiction to maintain the corporate existence and tax-exempt status of the Company; and the Company shall indemnify its directors and officers to the fullest extent permitted by the Act.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the undersigned directors have signed these resolutions as of the date first above written.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Office within the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) of the Cook Islands; FSC e-Registry online portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The applicant, through a licensed Cook Islands Registered Agent, submits a name clearance application stating the proposed corporate name in Latin script and confirming the name is not identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered entity or protected name. The Registrar issues a written availability confirmation and reserves the name for a period of 60 days pending full incorporation.
required_dossiers: Name Clearance / Reservation Request (Form IC-0)
Certified copy of passport of each ultimate beneficial owner
Certificate of good standing of corporate parent (if applicable)
Registered agent engagement letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on grounds of similarity, prohibited words, or public policy, the applicant may file an alternative name within 10 business days or submit a written appeal to the Registrar under s. 5 of the ICA supported by a statutory declaration of distinctiveness and evidence of laches or consent from the objecting entity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FSC-licensed Registered Agent (statutory incorporation intermediary); FSC e-Registry pre-drafting review.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Registered Agent prepares the Articles of Incorporation (Form IC-1) and consents (Forms IC-2 and IC-3), setting out company name, authorized share capital and share classes, registered office address, initial directors, and the authorized business purpose. The sole incorporator executes the Articles and the directors sign consents; signatures may be delivered electronically through a secure e-signature platform, and each director's and beneficial owner's identity is verified by notarized passports and proof of residential address.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation (Form IC-1) fully executed
Consents of Directors (Form IC-2)
Consent and Acceptance of Registered Agent (Form IC-3)
Notarized passport copies of all directors and shareholders
Proof of residential/business address (utility bill or bank reference, dated within 3 months)
AML/KYC questionnaire and source-of-funds declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar requests amendments, the Registered Agent may file amended Articles within 15 working days without losing priority; where non-compliance concerns identity verification, supplementary independent electronic verification or a bank reference letter may be lodged to cure the deficiency.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Financial Supervisory Commission of the Cook Islands; FSC e-Registry.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Registered Agent lodges Form IC-1 together with Forms IC-2 and IC-3 and the government incorporation fee (NZD 500, approximately USD 300) and the initial annual levy through the FSC e-Registry. The Registrar reviews the application, registers the company in the International Companies Register, and issues the Certificate of Incorporation, which is conclusive evidence of corporate existence.
required_dossiers: Form IC-1 (Articles of Incorporation) with Registrar's filing receipt
Forms IC-2 and IC-3 (consents)
AML/KYC file of beneficial owners
Evidence of payment of government fees and annual levy
Declaration that shares are beneficially owned by non-residents of the Cook Islands
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or suspended, the Registered Agent is given 20 working days to submit curative documentation or written representations; upon refusal, the applicant may re-file a corrected application or appeal to the Registrar and subsequently to the FSC Board under the ICA's review provisions, with no additional incorporation fee payable on re-filing within the statutory period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies; FSC-licensed Registered Agent.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation, the Registered Agent obtains a certified copy from the Registrar, passes the company seal, minute book, share certificates and registers of members/directors to the company, and uploads the electronic version to the client portal. The issued share certificates are prepared in the name of the sole beneficial owner.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation (original or certified copy)
Register of Members and Register of Directors
Share certificate(s)
Company minute book and common seal
Incumbency certificate signed by the Registered Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a certificate or register contains a clerical error, the Registered Agent files a written request for administrative correction with the Registrar, and a corrected certificate or register entry is issued within 5 business days at no additional government fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of First Board Resolutions and Governance Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Company (acting by unanimous written resolution); filed in the company's registered office records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The first board of directors adopts the pro forma first board resolutions covering adoption of the Articles, allotment of shares, establishment of the registered office, appointment of directors and officers, confirmation of the tax-exempt business scope, and authorization of banking and payment-rail onboarding. The resolutions are signed by all directors and filed in the company's statutory records; an incumbency certificate is issued to evidence authority of officers.
required_dossiers: Signed first board resolutions
Written consents of directors
Incumbency certificate
Register of directors and officers
Share allotment journal and register of members entries
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any governance record is found defective or incomplete, the directors may execute a curative unanimous written resolution, and the corrected minutes or registers are backdated only to the extent permitted by the Act; missing signatures are obtained and notarially attested, with the correction notice noted in the minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Exemption Confirmation and Annual Return Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies (annual return); Treasury, Ministry of Finance and Economic Management of the Cook Islands (tax administration).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Registered Agent files the first annual return within 30 days after the anniversary of incorporation, confirms the non-resident status of the beneficial owner, and pays the annual government levy. No income tax return is required to be filed because the company is statutorily exempt from Cook Islands income tax; the company must, however, continue to avoid carrying on business with Cook Islands residents and avoid deriving income from Cook Islands sources.
required_dossiers: Annual Return (Form IC-AR)
Updated register of directors and beneficial owners
Declaration of continued non-resident ownership
Receipt of payment of the annual government levy
Compliance letter from the Registered Agent confirming no local business activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual return is filed late, a late filing penalty applies and the company may be struck off; the remedy is to file the overdue return with the Registrar under the late-filing remediation policy, pay the imposed penalty, and, where a strike-off has occurred, apply for reinstatement within the statutory period with evidence that the company remained solvent and did not carry on Cook Islands business.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Onboarding of Payment Rails (Stripe and Wise)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Stripe, Inc. (payments compliance team); Wise US Inc. / Wise Platform (commercial onboarding); subject to the laws of the payment processor's jurisdiction.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The company's officers submit the incorporation package to Stripe and Wise through their business onboarding interfaces: Certificate of Incorporation, Articles, incumbency certificate, register of directors, beneficial owner passports, business plan describing automated subtitle transcription and AI voice cloning services, and confirmation of compliance with acceptable-use and anti-fraud policies. The company identifies the payment settlement currency (USD) and connects its bank account or prepares for settlement to a beneficiary bank account.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of incumbency
Register of directors and beneficial ownership declarations
Passport and address verification of signatories and UBOs
Service description and terms of service for AI dubbing/subtitling platform
Compliance declarations on prohibited content, voice-cloning consent, and IP ownership
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the payment processor requests enhanced due diligence, the company shall provide source-of-funds evidence, client contracts, and a supplementary AML questionnaire; if the account remains rejected, the company may submit a written appeal to the processor's compliance board, or alternatively apply for onboarding through a licensed payment facilitator, maintaining the right to designate additional processors without registration in the Cook Islands.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, Environmental and Occupational Licensing (Physical Studio Track)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Trade Licensing Authority, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Immigration; National Environment Service (NES); Fire and Emergency Services authority; Ministry of Infrastructure (Cook Islands).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the company elects to establish a physical studio or office, it applies for a Business Licence (Category: Commercial/Trade Service), obtains a building code compliance certificate from the Ministry of Infrastructure, passes a fire safety inspection, and registers with the National Environment Service for a Class B environmental registration. If the company operates purely remotely and offshore, no physical licensing is required and a written exemption confirmation may be obtained from the Business Trade Licensing Authority.
required_dossiers: Business Licence Application (Form BL-01) and applicable fee
Lease agreement or certificate of title for premises
Building code compliance certificate
Fire safety inspection certificate
NES Class B Environment Registration form
Occupational health and safety statement and staff induction records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A refused or conditioned Business Licence may be appealed to the Registrar of Business Licenses within 15 days, and a further appeal lies to the Minister. Environmental registration decisions may be appealed to the National Environment Council within 21 days, and building/fire clearance deficiencies may be cured by engaging licensed contractors and submitting revised compliance certificates to the relevant inspectorate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Business Trade Licensing Authority, Department of Trade, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Immigration of the Cook Islands; for an offshore-only international company transacting exclusively with non-residents, no local industrial license is required, but a written exemption confirmation may be obtained from the same authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Licence (Category: Commercial/Trade Service) under the Business Licensing Act 2012 (Cook Islands); the specific business of AI subtitle transcription, voice cloning and dubbing is not a separately licensed media activity under Cook Islands law. Where the studio operates as a pure digital/offshore enterprise, the applicable status is a written general exemption from the Business Licence requirement.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: National Environment Service (NES) of the Cook Islands, operating under the Environment Act 2003.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class B – Environment Registration (activity-specific) for a physical studio with office equipment, servers, or small-scale generator use; a Full EIA Report (Class A – EIA Consent) is not anticipated for post-production media services unless a high-consumption data center or significant waste stream is established. Purely cloud-hosted/remote AI transcription operations are categorised as exempt from NES registration.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Physical studio: wastewater from any kitchen, sanitary, or cooling systems must meet the Environment Act 2003 s. 22 discharge consent standards and the NES Water Quality Guidelines (no untreated trade waste, pH 6.5-8.5, BOD not exceeding 20 mg/L, suspended solids not exceeding 30 mg/L unless otherwise consented). Backup generator emissions must comply with ambient air-quality screening levels for NOx, SO2, PM10, and VOCs; refrigerants and fire-suppression agents must be ozone-depleting-substance compliant. E-waste (GPUs, computers, monitors) must be handled through the NES-approved e-waste collection and export pathway under the Basel Convention transboundary movement controls, and solid general waste must be collected by the Ministry of Infrastructure solid-waste service. For digital-only operations: no discharge or emissions thresholds apply at the company site, but cloud providers must maintain ISO 14001 (or equivalent) environmental management certification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate under the Fire Service Act 2012 (Cook Islands) issued by the Cook Islands Fire and Emergency Services, including verified fire detection, suppression, and means-of-egress for any premises. Structural load and building compliance certificate under the Building Act 2010 (Cook Islands), administered by the Ministry of Infrastructure, covering seismic resilience, electrical safety (wiring certificate per Electric Power Supply Regulations), and accessibility. Occupational health and safety clearance under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2018 (Cook Islands), requiring a documented workplace safety policy, first-aid arrangements, office ergonomics and screen-based workstation assessment, and an emergency evacuation plan approved by civil defense authorities.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) — officially 'Inland Revenue' / 'Te Tari Taake'; statutory digital portal is 'myIR' (https://www.ird.govt.nz), with parallel business identity registration via the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) portal (https://www.nzbn.govt.nz) operated by the Companies Office under the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Obtain an NZBN if the CK_IC International Company is incorporated in New Zealand, carries on a taxable activity in New Zealand, or has a physical place of business in New Zealand; if the company is wholly offshore and has no NZ taxable activity, an NZBN is not a prerequisite. Step 2: Submit Form IR596 (Non-Resident Company IRD Number Application) or, where the company is close-held, Form IR742, to Inland Revenue via a registered New Zealand tax agent, by post, or through the myIR non-resident entity registration channel. The application must include a certified copy of the certificate of incorporation, the constitution/articles of association, the register of directors and shareholders, and a declaration of the entity's tax residence and permanent establishment status. Step 3: Upon issuance of the IRD number, the entity must assess GST registration obligations: if total taxable supplies in any rolling 12-month period are expected to exceed NZD 60,000 — including remote services (e.g., automated subtitle transcription, AI voice dubbing) supplied to New Zealand consumers — the company must apply to register for GST in myIR. Step 4: Register for PAYE, FBT, and KiwiSaver only if the IC obtains New Zealand resident employees; for a purely offshore service desk with non-resident contractors, no payroll registration is required. Step 5: Appoint an authorised agent in New Zealand for service of notices where the company has no fixed establishment; this is administratively recommended and does not in itself create a permanent establishment. No minimum capital subscription or local bank account is required for IRD number issuance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — The CK_IC (International Company) is classified as a non-resident company under section YD 2 of the Income Tax Act 2007, with central management and control outside New Zealand and no New Zealand permanent establishment. The company is taxable only on New Zealand-sourced income that is effectively connected with a New Zealand taxable activity (sections YD 4, BD 1); all foreign-source trading profits, including revenue from offshore post-production, subtitle transcription, and AI voice-dubbing services delivered to foreign clients, fall entirely outside the New Zealand tax net and are non-assessable and exempt. The Tax_Exempt_Zone status does not automatically confer fiscal transparency; absent a valid Look-Through Company election, the entity is liable at the 28% corporate rate only on any NZ-sourced business income, has no New Zealand capital duty, no wealth tax, no stamp duty, and no branch profit remittance tax. As a pure non-resident with no NZ-sourced income, the effective NZ tax liability is nil.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: (1) Look-Through Company (LTC) election under Subpart HB of the Income Tax Act 2007: a close-held company (five or fewer ultimate shareholders, no corporate shareholder) may elect to be fiscally transparent, with profits and losses attributed to shareholders — the functional equivalent of a US check-the-box election; the election is effected via form IR861 and requires all shareholders to sign. (2) GST group election under section 55 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985: permits a non-resident IC and its New Zealand GST-registered related entities to file a single consolidated GST return. (3) CFC branch-equivalent and de minimis elections under Subparts CQ/EX of the Income Tax Act 2007: available to New Zealand-resident shareholders to mitigate attribution on controlled foreign companies; not relevant to the CK_IC itself but relevant to any NZ-resident parent. (4) Trans-Tasman branch election for Australian-resident companies to be treated as having a New Zealand permanent establishment; not applicable to the Cook Islands-style IC absent an Australian nexus. (5) Hybrid mismatch elections: New Zealand does not provide a discretionary 'check-the-box' for hybrid entities; instead, the hybrid and branch mismatch rules in Part FM (sections FM 1–FM 16) and the investor/group mismatch rules in Subparts FH and FO operate mandatorily to deny deductions or impose withholding tax to neutralise double non-taxation. No special statutory election is required to activate the Tax_Exempt_Zone status; it arises automatically from non-residence and absence of NZ-sourced taxable activity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) — Goods and Services Tax Act 1985; administered by Inland Revenue as a single-stage, broad-based consumption tax on supplies of goods and services made in New Zealand, including imported remote services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 (annual taxable supplies in any rolling 12-month period; the same threshold applies to both resident suppliers and non-resident suppliers of 'remote services' — including digital post-production, automated subtitle transcription, and AI voice-dubbing services — supplied to GST-registered New Zealand businesses and New Zealand consumers; once the threshold is exceeded, registration is compulsory within 21 days; voluntary registration is available to non-residents, but input tax recovery is limited to supplies attributable to New Zealand taxable activities).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand operates a voluntary PAN-NZ e-invoicing framework based on the PEPPOL BIS 3.0 specification (NZ e-Invoicing, supported by MyInvoicing and other PEPPOL access points). There is no real-time fiscal clearance regime, no government pre-clearance API, no mandatory digital stamping, and no continuous transaction controls with Inland Revenue. All registered suppliers, including the CK_IC, must issue a GST tax invoice within 28 days of the time of supply (section 24, GST Act 1985); the invoice must contain the supplier's name, GST number, issue date, description, consideration, and the GST-inclusive/exclusive amounts. Zero-rated export invoices must contain an explicit statement that the supply is zero-rated and the basis for that treatment. E-invoicing becomes mandatory only for suppliers transacting with certain central government agencies; no private-sector mandate currently exists. Inland Revenue performs ex-post data-matching audit analysis rather than transaction-level clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under sections 11 and 11A of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, the CK_IC may claim 0% GST on: (a) goods physically exported from New Zealand by the supplier within 28 days of the supply (or within such longer period as the Commissioner allows); (b) services supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand at the time the services are performed, provided the services are not supplied to any person in New Zealand in connection with the same supply — this covers automated subtitle transcription, AI voice cloning, and audio dubbing delivered electronically to offshore film studios, streaming platforms, and foreign distributors; (c) 'remote services' (electronically supplied services) received by a non-resident who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply, where the recipient's GST registration is not being used in connection with the supply; and (d) services that are directly connected with movable property that is outside New Zealand when the services are performed. Zero-rating is denied where the service is supplied to a New Zealand resident, where the services relate to land in New Zealand, where the services are performed while the recipient is physically present in New Zealand, or where the supply is part of a deliberate scheme to avoid GST. Evidence of non-residency includes the customer's overseas address, IP address, bank jurisdiction, and contractual warranties.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration filed electronically via the Trade Single Window / New Zealand Customs Service (required only for physical media, master files on tangible carriers, or any accompanying physical deliverables; for pure digital delivery, a goods export declaration is not applicable and the documented digital delivery trail stands in its place)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill (for tangible export of mastered files or physical promotional materials; must be dated within the statutory zero-rating window)
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) issued by a New Zealand registered bank confirming settlement in foreign currency and the receipt of export proceeds into the IC's offshore or onshore account
Zero-rated GST tax invoice and the underlying service agreement/PO with the non-resident client, including the client's overseas jurisdiction of establishment and warranty of non-residence

Technical delivery logs, IP geolocation evidence, and email/digital handover records demonstrating that the subtitle and AI-voice deliverables were supplied to, and used by, a recipient outside New Zealand
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Inland Revenue applies targeted compliance scrutiny to zero-rated export claims by small offshore-facing entities, including verification of the non-resident status of the recipient, the place of supply, and the receipt of foreign currency. Where a zero-rating claim is unsupported or the Commissioner establishes a deliberate arrangement to mischaracterise domestic supplies as exports, the following consequences arise under the Tax Administration Act 1994 and the GST Act 1985: (1) reversal of the zero-rating with a default assessment of GST at 15%, plus use-of-money interest from the original due date; (2) shortfall penalties under section 141: 20% for 'lack of reasonable care', 40% for 'unacceptable tax position', and up to 150% for 'tax evasion' or 'obstructive conduct'; (3) an additional 100% 'abusive tax position' penalty may be stacked where the dominant purpose is to defeat the intent of the GST Act; (4) criminal prosecution in the District Court for knowingly filing false GST returns, with fines up to NZD 50,000 for each offence and potential imprisonment under section 143A of the Tax Administration Act 1994; (5) the promoter penalty regime under section 43A can reach promoters of fraudulent export schemes with penalties of up to NZD 100,000; and (6) retrospective clawback of any GST refunds paid, with statutory interest accruing. For the CK_IC, the safest posture is to maintain the full documentation bundle, evidence foreign currency settlement, and comply with the 180-day repatriation benchmark to avoid any inference of unreturned export proceeds or sham exportation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility is the baseline: New Zealand operates a free-floating, market-determined NZD regime with no exchange-control licensing and no distinction between current and capital account approvals. For a non-resident-owned International Company in the Realm of New Zealand, invoicing out of NZD or USD, profit repatriation, intercompany loans, and service-fee remittances may proceed without RBNZ clearance. The operative constraints are non-FX filters: (i) the Overseas Investment Act 2005 applies only to sensitive land or significant business assets, not to post-production AI services; (ii) Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) at 15% applies to outbound dividends unless reduced by an applicable double-tax agreement; and (iii) bank-level AML/CFT documentation of source of funds is mandatory.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory surrender rules in New Zealand. Export proceeds from subtitle transcription and AI dubbing services may be retained indefinitely in foreign currency, converted at any time at commercial interbank rates, or offset against import disbursements. No mandatory conversion ratio or time limit exists; the only practical requirement is accurate BOP/transaction purpose codes captured by the collecting bank for statistical reporting.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Business Transactional Account with Global Trade and FX Facilities
Corporate Operational Account and Treasury Workspace

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High as a payment gateway, Medium as a stand-alone liquidity rail. Wise and Stripe are compliant Financial Service Providers (FSP) in New Zealand under the Financial Service Providers (Registration and Disputes Resolution) Act 2008 and are eligible for account-to-account payouts, but they are not registered banks under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021 and therefore cannot hold long-term concentration risk, structured deposits, or provide letters of credit. Legal constraint: all remittances must be linked to identifiable underlying transactions to satisfy AML/CFT custody obligations; they are best used as collection rails with daily sweeps into a tier-1 bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory universal in-person mandate exists in New Zealand law; each bank sets its own onboarding policy. For low-AML-risk entities, remote video KYC with notarised/apostilled corporate documents is usually accepted. However, if the shareholder structure is a Cook Islands-style Trust or International Company (CK_IC), the benchmark expectation is: (i) physical or video attendance of at least one director authorised by resolution; (ii) original certification of the Certificate of Incorporation, Incumbency and Registered Agent Declaration; and (iii) proof of the principal operating address in New Zealand. Where physical appearance is impractical, an Apostilled certified copy set prepared through the New Zealand High Commission is the fallback defence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident International Company (CK_IC) with offshore trust ownership and no New Zealand employees.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Certificate of Incorporation and Constitution; Register of Directors and Incumbency Certificate issued by the registered agent; trust deed or UBO schedule transparently naming settlor, trustee and beneficiaries; New Zealand registered office agreement; statement of economic substance demonstrating commercial activity management.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: A short history of high-volume digital inflows from Stripe/Wise without formal purchase orders.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Licensed payment-platform settlement statements; customer invoices and machine-generated subtitle service records; signed platform terms with payout entity mapping; monthly GL extracts and intercompany reconciliation log.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border counterparty exposure to high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Screening certificates against UN/OFAC/European Union and NZ consolidated sanctions lists; risk-rated counterparty CDD file; restrictive jurisdictional policy showing refusal of dealers in embargoed territories; external due diligence reports on major clients.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficiary-name mismatches arising from AI licensing platform aggregation (payment under a holding nominee instead of the CK_IC).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Disclosed agency agreements and DBA registrations; upstream platform settlement policies; audited consolidated receivable ledger; director attestation and foreign-law opinion on nominee collection.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant route: SWIFT MT103 with beneficiary = CK_IC and New Zealand bank account, purpose code clearly indicating 'Direct investment - Equity injection' or 'Shareholder loan' (BOP service group for current-account advances). Include a board resolution authorising the transfer, a signed loan deed if structured as debt, and the bank's own FX reference for NZD conversion. The NZD leg clears through the Reserve Bank's ESAS high-value settlement system; USD legs can be sent via CHIPS or Fedwire to the NZ bank's correspondent.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For royalty and post-production vendor payments: SWIFT MT103 / MT202 COV across the licensed correspondent network; USD disbursements settle over CHIPS/Fedwire, EUR over TARGET2, and GBP over CHAPS. Domestic NZD vendor runs settle over the Exchange Settlement Account System (ESAS). A Commercial Letter of Credit is not standard for AI subtitle services; where mastering hardware is physically imported, a standby LC or DP arrangement with transport documents is permissible but unnecessary for pure software delivery.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright forward contracts (typically up to 12 months)
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps for long-term intercompany funding
Vanilla FX options for earnings protection
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible emerging-market destination currencies only

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Companies Act 1993, s 214) confirming registered office, directors, shareholding, and company status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing due on the anniversary of incorporation; must be submitted within 20 working days after the anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 50 (approx USD 31); failure to file after Registrar notice may trigger administrative strike-off from the New Zealand Companies Register within 20 working days; directors may face disqualification and personal liability for continued trading

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit applies to large companies (total assets > NZD 33 million or revenue > NZD 10 million, or a parent of such an entity); small and mid-size entities are exempt unless shareholders holding 10% or more request an audit; FMC reporting entities must also comply
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand IFRS (including Reduced Disclosure Regime) and New Zealand GAAP prescribed by the External Reporting Board under the XRB A1 framework; local GAAP is accepted for small and medium-sized companies

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand has no separate annual UBO filing; changes in ownership are recorded in the Register of Members within 10 working days of any transfer and are reflected in the Annual Return; AML/CFT compliance requires ongoing beneficial ownership verification and risk assessment updates

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 – USD 15,000 per annum for a small to mid-size private company
